subject: Sanotech POC: environment decision, success metrics & kickoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sanotech.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@sanotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sanotech POC: environment decision, success metrics & kickoff

Hi Alyssa / Kevin — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposal so we can lock the trial environment and timeline.

TL;DR: We recommend a 4-week POC with two gating decisions: (A) environment topology (hosted sandbox vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial) and (B) success criteria for model accuracy/latency and allowed data flows. Please confirm preferred environment and any hard constraints by EOD Tue so we can schedule infra work.

Summary of objectives (from our call):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for clinical note summarization pipeline (PHI-handling required).
- Primary success metrics: mean ROUGE-L >= 0.48 on evaluation set; 95th percentile latency < 300ms for 512 token responses; no data egress outside authorized VPC.
- Secondary: integration with existing Kafka event stream and token-level cost estimate < $0.02 per 1k tokens.

Environment options (proposal):
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest): Redwood-managed hosted model endpoints. Pros: fastest to spin up, no infra work. Cons: not suitable if you require VPC-only controls or on-prem data residency.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): Redwood-managed hardware in a dedicated pool for your account. Pros: predictable throughput and isolation. Cons: longer lead time for capacity reservation; still uses Redwood control plane.
3) VPC trial (preferred if PHI): Customer VPC peering + Redwood private deployment pattern. Pros: private networking, customer-controlled subnets and routing, KMS integration. Cons: requires networking coordination and security onboarding.

Proposed immediate next steps / owners:
- S1: Sanotech confirms environment preference and any strict networking rules (Alyssa / Kevin) — due 2026-10-06.
- S2: Redwood security provides SOC2 evidence + network gating checklist (Marissa) — target 2026-10-04.
- S3: Infra kickoff to provision trial baseline and sample data ingest (Ben) — tentative start 2026-10-11.
- S4: Joint kickoff meeting to align test dataset, evaluation harness and access (Jordan) — propose 2026-10-12.

I attached the trial scope spreadsheet and a one-page POC matrix to show how we'll measure each criterion. If VPC is required, please attach your network contacts and security questionnaire as soon as possible.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sanotech_trial_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_poc_matrix.pdf (one-page matrix)

From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sanotech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@sanotech.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sanotech POC: environment decision, success metrics & kickoff

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick answers from our side:
- Environment preference: VPC trial. We have strict PHI controls and cannot allow production patient data to leave our VPC without explicit controls.
- Security asks: can you provide SOC2 Type II report, network ports/egress list, and an example audit log output? We attached our security questionnaire with items we typically need completed.
- Timeline: the team can meet for kickoff the week of 10/12; we prefer earlier (10/12 or 10/13).

Open questions:
- Will Redwood require a VPN or is AWS VPC peering supported?
- For the POC, can we scope to de-identified sample data first, then ramp to a small PHI sample once network controls are validated?

I've attached the security questionnaire (SanoTech_security_q.pdf) — Ben/Marissa, please take a look and let us know what you need to answer.

Best,
Alyssa Park
Director of Data & Integrations, SanoTech
alyssa.park@sanotech.com
Attachments: SanoTech_security_q.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sanotech POC: environment decision, security asks and internal plan

Internal note (do not forward to SanoTech yet) — aligning on a pragmatic rollout:
- Recommendation: Accept the VPC trial but stage it. Week 1: Redwood-hosted private control plane + VPC peering for smoke tests with de-identified data. Week 2-4: Gradual ramp to PHI sample with KMS key/CMK integration, audit log verification, and canary traffic. If peering proves slow to establish, have a dedicated sandbox fallback configured to accept only de-identified flows.

Owners & immediate actions:
- Ben Carter: draft network gating checklist and list of supported peering patterns (AWS peering, Transit Gateway). Deliverable: network checklist doc by 2026-10-05 EOD.
- Marissa: pull SOC2 Type II extract & example audit log; coordinate security call with Sanotech security on 2026-10-06.
- Jordan: prepare evaluation harness (scoring script + example dataset) and calendar invite for 10/12.

Risk notes: time to get customers' security team to sign off is the critical path. We should propose a narrow PHI scope and a hard stop if audit logs/audit retention don't meet their policy. Also: call out that dedicated sandbox reservation may require a minimum 2-week lead time and we should avoid commits until after the kickoff.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@sanotech.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@sanotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Sanotech POC: confirmed next steps, invite & action owners

Following up — consolidated next steps and actions after internal alignment:
- Environment: VPC trial approved by Redwood (staged approach).
- Kickoff meeting: scheduled for 2026-10-12 10:00 PT — calendar invite sent separately (please accept).
- Action owners & deadlines:
  * Ben Carter: network gating checklist & supported peering patterns — due 2026-10-08.
  * Marissa Cole: SOC2 extract + example audit logs + security contact for 10/06 meeting — completed (doc in Drive).
  * Jordan Blake: evaluation harness (scoring script) + example dataset + updated trial scope spreadsheet — due 2026-10-09.
  * SanoTech (Alyssa): confirm final PHI scope (de-identified first, small PHI test later) and provide network contact — due 2026-10-06 (please confirm now).

Attachments: updated sanotech_trial_scope.xlsx (I added the staged plan and evaluation criteria).
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD_SANOTECH (trial artifacts), HubSpot deal SAN-1923.

Please reply if anything is missing or if the schedule doesn't work. We will not provision dedicated reserved capacity until we have a clear volume projection, but we will configure a dedicated sandbox as a fallback if needed.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Attachments: sanotech_trial_scope.xlsx
